title: BIAS, DIVERSITY, AND CHALLENGES TO FAIRNESS IN CLASSIFICATION AND AUTOMATED TEXT ANALYSIS. From libraries to AI and back
benchmark_measurement: The paper analyzes representational bias in library classification systems, specifically the Dewey Decimal Classification (DDC). It examines how the DDC provides more granular categories for Christianity while grouping other faiths into a single, coarse 'Other Religions' category. It also discusses how different religious holidays are cataloged in disparate sections, disadvantaging non-Christian faiths.
findings: The paper finds that traditional library classification systems like the Dewey Decimal Classification (DDC) exhibit structural bias against non-Christian religions. DDC offers seven detailed sub-categories for Christianity but groups all other faiths into a single 'Other religions' category, making non-Christian content less visible and nuanced. An example highlights how a librarian observed that Christian holidays were categorized under 'Social Sciences', while holidays from other faiths (Eid, Rosh Hashanah, Diwali) were placed under 'Other Religions', prompting a manual re-organization to ensure fairness for a diverse student population.
